papers.title: Label-free multi-metric pipeline for reproducible clustering of single-cell RNA-seq cell types.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed our ability to identify cell types and explore cellular diversity. However, determining whether apparent cell subtypes represent true biological populations or artifacts of data analysis remains a major challenge. To address this issue, we developed scClustBench, an open-source benchmarking framework that evaluates cluster quality, stability, and reproducibility across multiple analytical approaches. Rather than relying on a single clustering method, scClustBench tests whether proposed cell subtypes can be consistently recovered. We applied scClustBen
papers.journal: Life science alliance
papers.summary: The authors present scClustBench, an open-source benchmarking framework that evaluates single-cell RNA-seq clustering by testing cluster quality, stability, and reproducibility across multiple analytical approaches rather than relying on a single method. By checking whether proposed cell subtypes can be consistently recovered, the tool helps distinguish true biological populations from analysis artifacts.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omic mapping of urinary and intrarenal immune landscapes in lupus nephritis identifies convergent inflammatory and fibrotic programs.
papers.abstract: Renal biopsy is the gold standard for classifying lupus nephritis (LN), but due to its invasiveness and difficult longitudinal follow-up, it incompletely captures immune and histopathological dynamics. Urinary single-cell transcriptomic analysis has been proposed as a minimally invasive approach for monitoring LN, while renal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics provide high-resolution reference maps of the intrarenal environment. We performed a systematic scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to evaluate direct urinary-renal transcriptomic concordance and pathway molecular converg
papers.journal: Journal of translational autoimmunity
papers.summary: This scoping review examines how well urinary single-cell transcriptomics reflects the intrarenal immune landscape in lupus nephritis, comparing urine-based profiles with renal single-cell and spatial transcriptomic reference maps. The authors find evidence for convergent inflammatory and fibrotic programs across urinary and intrarenal compartments, supporting urine as a minimally invasive window into kidney pathology. The work highlights both the promise and current limitations of urinary transcriptomics for longitudinal LN monitoring.

papers.title: CD44+ Proximal Tubular Epithelial Cells May Be Involved in Renal Fibrosis and Inflammation via TGF-β Signaling in Hyperuricemic Nephropathy.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of hyperuricemia (HUA) is continuously increasing and HUA may eventually develop into irreversible hyperuricemic nephropathy (HN). Injured proximal tubule (PT) in the HUA microenvironment plays an important role in the progression of HN. However, the underlying pathological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between HUA kidneys and control groups were screened from bulk RNA sequencing data to identify abnormally activated signaling. Subsequently, PT cell-subtypes related to injury and repair were identified in single-cell RNA sequenc
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: Using bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, the authors identify a CD44+ proximal tubular epithelial cell subpopulation that is expanded in hyperuricemic nephropathy and appears to drive renal fibrosis and inflammation through TGF-β signaling. The study links hyperuricemia-induced tubular injury to a specific cell state and a candidate signaling pathway, suggesting a possible therapeutic target.

papers.title: Generating scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq using a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides detailed, genome-wide gene expression profiles at single-cell resolution, enabling the identification of disease-driving cell types and genes. However, scRNA-seq remains costly, and there are extremely limited samples generated in even the most extensive human disease studies. In contrast, bulk RNA-seq data is abundant but averages gene expression across all cell types, losing cell-specific detail. To further leverage this abundance of RNA-seq data, methods have been developed to infer cell type proportions and average expression from bulk data u
papers.journal: PLoS computational biology
papers.summary: The authors present a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder that reconstructs single-cell-resolution gene expression profiles from bulk RNA-seq data. By modeling cell type proportions and cell-type-specific expression, the method aims to recover cell-level detail that is otherwise averaged out in bulk samples, allowing existing bulk datasets to be mined for single-cell information.

papers.title: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues.
papers.abstract: Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. However, proteome mapping technologies lag far behind other transcriptome (genome) mapping technologies. Here we report an Ultralow-volume, Shallow, Microwell plate-based voxel Collection and Processing coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) method, termed USMCP-MS, for robust scalable proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions. This method was built upon the design of
papers.journal: Nature communications
papers.summary: The authors present USMCP-MS, a method that uses shallow microwell plates to collect and process ultralow-volume tissue voxels for mass-spectrometry-based spatial proteome mapping. This addresses the lag of spatial proteomics behind spatial transcriptomics, enabling scalable, high-resolution mapping of tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment.

papers.title: Spatially Resolved Transcriptomic Correlation Improves the Prediction of Anticancer Drug Candidates.
papers.abstract: Predicting the anticancer effects of compounds is critical for computational drug evaluation. However, traditional transcriptomics-based virtual screening relies on bulk RNA profiling, causing intratumoral spatial heterogeneity to be averaged across the entire tissue and thereby limiting predictive accuracy. This limitation is particularly consequential for triple-negative breast cancer, which lacks receptor-guided treatment options and exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity that can obscure region-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities when assessed by bulk analysis alone. To address this li
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors propose a virtual screening approach that uses spatially resolved transcriptomics instead of bulk RNA profiling to predict anticancer drug candidates, arguing that bulk data averages away intratumoral spatial heterogeneity. They apply this to triple-negative breast cancer, where spatial heterogeneity is pronounced and receptor-guided options are lacking, aiming to capture region-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities. The work suggests that incorporating spatial correlation structure improves prediction accuracy over conventional transcriptomics-based screening.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomics reveal fibroblast-monocyte crosstalk with JAK-STAT activation associated with Parvimonas micra-induced periodontitis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to characterize the spatial and molecular mechanisms of Parvimonas micra-induced periodontitis, which remains poorly understood. We used bulk RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to investigate gingival responses in ligature and P. micra-induced rat periodontitis model and validated the findings in human patients. In rat periodontitis model, significant transcriptomic changes occurred across gingival regions, especially in the suprabasal epithelium, affecting autophagy and immune defense. Both bulk and spatial transcriptomic analyses indicate that JAK-STAT signaling was
papers.journal: mSystems
papers.summary: Using bulk and spatial transcriptomics in a rat periodontitis model, the authors show that Parvimonas micra infection drives region-specific gingival transcriptomic changes, particularly in suprabasal epithelium affecting autophagy and immune defense. Integrated analyses reveal fibroblast-monocyte crosstalk with JAK-STAT pathway activation, which was validated in human periodontitis patients. The work implicates a specific microbial species and cell-cell signaling axis in disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: AI-driven multi-omics identifies SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a therapeutic target and predicts lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spat
papers.journal: NPJ precision oncology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a driver of lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer. The authors functionally validate these macrophages as a therapeutic target and develop a predictive model for metastasis. The work demonstrates how AI-driven multi-omics can uncover targetable cell populations and improve metastasis prediction.

papers.title: Identification of immune pathways regulating the cell mediated immunity in leishmaniasis in humans.
papers.abstract: A delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) response induced by the intradermal inoculation of leishmanin antigen induced in individuals exposed to parasite Leishmania is a reliable indicator of cell mediated immunity (CMI). Leishmanin antigen skin test (LST) is also an important tool in disease surveillance studies in endemic area and can be used to assess vaccine efficacy. Previous studies assessing CMI in Leishmania exposed individuals were limited to analysis of PBMCs. To investigate the mediators of CMI, we performed spatial transcriptomic analysis of the DTH skin biopsies after leishmanin anti
papers.journal: PLoS neglected tropical diseases
papers.summary: The authors used spatial transcriptomics to profile skin biopsies from leishmanin skin tests, which elicit a delayed-type hypersensitivity response reflecting cell-mediated immunity in people exposed to Leishmania parasites. This moves beyond prior PBMC-based studies by mapping immune mediators directly in the tissue microenvironment of the DTH reaction, identifying immune pathways that regulate cell-mediated immunity in human leishmaniasis.

papers.title: Homeostatic fibroblast niche collapse in clinically uninvolved skin defines a subclinical state of systemic sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, or scleroderma, is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by vasculopathy, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. Heterogeneous clinical presentation and polygenic risk complicate our understanding of disease mechanisms and the path to effective therapy. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses have revealed substantial heterogeneity in skin, but disease-associated reprogramming remains poorly defined. To address this, we performed high-resolution spatial transcriptomic profiling of paired clinically uninvolved and clinically affected
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used high-resolution spatial transcriptomics to compare clinically unaffected versus affected skin in systemic sclerosis patients. The key finding is that even clinically uninvolved skin shows a collapse of the homeostatic fibroblast niche, defining a subclinical disease state that precedes visible fibrosis. This suggests that fibroblast niche disruption is an early, spatially organized event in scleroderma pathogenesis.

papers.title: Iterative Geometric Structure Guided Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Scheme for Bulk Tissue RNA-seq Data Deconvolution.
papers.abstract: Complete deconvolution is a class of unsupervised methods that aim to estimate both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles (GEPs) from bulk RNA-seq data, without requiring prior reference profiles. Hence, it enables broader applicability to tissues or species for which reference data are limited or unavailable. For many existing methods, nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) serves as the fundamental computational tool. However, NMF is mathematically ill-posed and a comprehensive understanding of how to overcome the inherent ill-posedness and improve solution ac
papers.journal: Bulletin of mathematical biology
papers.summary: This paper proposes an iterative geometric structure-guided nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) method for complete deconvolution of bulk RNA-seq data, estimating both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles without reference profiles. The approach addresses the mathematical ill-posedness of standard NMF by incorporating geometric structure to constrain and improve the solution. This enables deconvolution in tissues or species where reference data are limited or unavailable.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses characterize an IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern in extracellular matrix remodeling and Treg-associated immune suppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is characterized by extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. As an important N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its downstream regulatory network and potential role in immune microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Neoplasia (New York, N.Y.)
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to show that the m6A reader IGF2BP3 promotes extracellular matrix remodeling and Treg-mediated immune suppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma, acting through MMP7. The work links an RNA-binding protein to both matrix remodeling and immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important cha
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces st2sc, a computational method for recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses the challenge of deconvolving spot-level signals by explicitly identifying individual cells and accurately estimating per-gene expression, improving on existing approaches that struggle with gene-level accuracy.

papers.title: ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D Are associated with urea cycle activity and ammonia stress responses in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PRAD) progression is closely associated with metabolic reprogramming, but the role of nitrogen metabolism and ammonia-associated cell death remains unclear. This study investigates the clinical and functional significance of urea cycle activity in PRAD.
papers.journal: Neoplasia (New York, N.Y.)
papers.summary: This study examines how urea cycle activity and ammonia-related stress responses contribute to prostate cancer progression. The authors identify ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D as genes associated with these metabolic processes, suggesting a link between nitrogen metabolism and prostate cancer biology.

papers.title: Aging drives senescence in visceral adipose to a greater extent than obesity, instigating multicellular common signaling patterns that impair organ function and drive inflammation.
papers.abstract: Obesity accelerates key hallmarks of biological aging in visceral adipose tissue (VAT), yet age-associated changes in cellular senescence against a background of sustained elevated adiposity remain poorly understood. To investigate these changes, we examined human omental VAT from younger (18-35 years), middle-aged (36-51 years), and older adults (52-75 years) with comparable BMI (40 ± 5 kg/m²) using a cross-sectional design. We integrated bulk and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), Visium HD spatial transcriptomics, and three complementary computational approaches for senescent cell (
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using bulk and single-nucleus RNA-seq plus Visium HD spatial transcriptomics on human omental visceral adipose tissue from adults with comparable high BMI across three age groups, the authors show that aging drives cellular senescence more strongly than obesity itself. Senescent cells appear to instigate shared multicellular signaling patterns that impair organ function and promote inflammation. The work highlights age, independent of adiposity, as a key driver of adipose dysfunction.

papers.title: Spindle: Scalable Indexing of Spatial-Omics Data for Fast Querying.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has unlocked new avenues for biological discovery by jointly capturing gene expression and spatial context. ST datasets are typically stored as gene expression matrices paired with spatial coordinates, supporting queries based on expression levels at individual locations. However, characterizing how genes vary together requires representations of relationships between genes, such as covariance matrices computed over spatial neighborhoods. These gene-gene co-expression patterns capture coordinated biological variation and can reveal spatially localized gene programs
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Spindle is a new indexing system for spatial transcriptomics data that enables fast querying of gene-gene co-expression patterns computed over spatial neighborhoods, rather than just expression at individual spots. This addresses a gap where existing storage formats only support location-based expression queries, not relationship-based queries needed to reveal spatially localized gene programs.

papers.title: A versatile set of computational tools for inference of genetic ancestry from human molecular data.
papers.abstract: Molecular properties of human diseases and conditions often exhibit dependence on the genetic ancestry of the donor. In order to make more human molecular data available for ancestry-informed research, we developed a set of software tools termed Robust Ancestry Inference using Data Synthesis (RAIDS) for inference of genetic ancestry from sequence data that pose challenges to genotyping. The data-synthesis procedure, underlying RAIDS, makes it a unique tool capable of assessing and optimizing the accuracy of inference for each individual molecular profile, with no resort to cohort data. Here we
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present RAIDS, a set of computational tools for inferring genetic ancestry from human molecular data, including sequence data that are difficult to genotype. RAIDS uses a data-synthesis approach that can assess and optimize ancestry inference accuracy for each individual sample without requiring cohort data.

papers.title: SigBridgeR: An R Toolkit for Standardized Identification and Benchmarking of Phenotype-Associated Cell Subpopulations in Single-Cell Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has revolutionized our understanding of cellular heterogeneity, yet linking specific cell subpopulations to clinically relevant phenotypes remains a major challenge. Although multiple computational methods have been developed to integrate bulk transcriptomic and single-cell data for phenotype-associated cell identification, differences in algorithmic strategies, parameter configurations, software implementations, and output formats make it difficult to compare methods fairly, reproduce analyses, and determine which approach is most suitable for a given bi
papers.journal: GigaScience
papers.summary: SigBridgeR is an R toolkit that standardizes the identification and benchmarking of phenotype-associated cell subpopulations by integrating bulk transcriptomic data with single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses the current fragmentation in the field, where diverse computational methods with different algorithms, parameters, and output formats make fair comparison and reproducibility difficult. The toolkit provides a unified framework for running, comparing, and benchmarking these methods.

papers.title: Subcellular Spatial Profiling Unveils Links Between Neuritic Plaques with Selective Tau Vulnerability in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) features widespread extracellular amyloid-β plaques but selective intraneuronal tau accumulation in cortical layers II/III and V, while layer IV remains relatively resistant. Here, we combined subcellular spatial transcriptomics with co-registered Aβ and pTau immunohistochemistry to determine why neurons exposed to comparable plaque-associated pathology differ in somatic pTau accumulation. Plaque-associated neuritic stress occurred similarly across layers, but layer IV neurons showed attenuated pTau accumulation and reduced somatic expression of a shared neurite-soma s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using subcellular spatial transcriptomics combined with co-registered amyloid-β and pTau immunohistochemistry, this study investigated why neurons in different cortical layers accumulate tau differently despite comparable plaque exposure. Plaque-associated neuritic stress occurred similarly across layers, but layer IV neurons showed attenuated somatic pTau accumulation and reduced expression of a shared neurite-to-soma signaling program, suggesting selective vulnerability is driven by somatic transcriptional responses rather than plaque proximity alone.

papers.title: Myeloid subpopulations correlate with responsiveness to therapy in a prospective, longitudinal study on RA patients.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease associated with the destruction of cartilage and bone, increased risk of cardiovascular disease and a higher mortality rate. Despite the many therapies that exist for RA, there is little information to guide selection of the most effective treatment for an individual patient. Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies have created an opportunity to investigate the target tissue. While a number of studies have characterized the stromal and immune cell populations using single-cell technology on synovial biopsy samples, here we performed a longitudinal
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal study used ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies to track myeloid cell subpopulations in rheumatoid arthritis patients over time and correlate them with treatment response. The authors identify specific myeloid subsets whose abundance associates with responsiveness to therapy, suggesting these could serve as biomarkers for guiding treatment selection. The work extends prior single-cell characterizations of synovial tissue by adding a longitudinal, treatment-response dimension.

papers.title: Spatial proteomics on repurposed sequencers reveals early astrocytic remodeling in an ALS mouse model.
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics can reveal how disease reshapes cells and their local environments, but extending these measurements across replicated tissue cohorts requires validated antibodies, consistent sample processing and integrated analysis. These requirements are particularly pressing in studies of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), where pathology evolves unevenly across spinal-cord regions and disease stages. Here, we established an end-to-end spatial proteomics workflow linking a validated 28-antibody panel to automated fluorescence decoding and imaging on repurposed high-throughput sequence
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed an end-to-end spatial proteomics workflow that uses repurposed high-throughput DNA sequencers for automated fluorescence decoding and imaging, paired with a validated 28-antibody panel. Applying this to an ALS mouse model, they detected early astrocytic remodeling in the spinal cord before overt disease pathology, demonstrating that scalable spatial proteomics can capture region- and stage-specific cellular changes across replicated tissue cohorts.

papers.title: A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans -regulatory architecture in the aging human brain.
papers.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans -QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap , a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans -QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans -eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors present TransMap, a computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Applied to the aging human brain, it constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes and yields a cell-type-resolved map of trans-regulatory architecture, addressing the poor reproducibility and weak effect sizes that have limited trans-QTL studies.

papers.title: SPACE-Tag Enables High-Throughput Spatial Chromatin Profiling With CUT&Tag.
papers.abstract: Spatial epigenomics maps chromatin states within intact tissues, yet current methods remain limited by accessibility and scale. We developed SPACE-Tag, a spatial CUT&Tag framework that converts epigenetic marks-associated DNA into polyadenylated RNA through T7-based linear amplification, enabling direct integration with standard spatial transcriptomic workflows. Applied to the mouse brain, SPACE-Tag resolved activating and repressive chromatin landscapes, recovered region-specific gene-regulatory programs across anatomical domains, and showed strong correlation with existing bulk and single-ce
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SPACE-Tag is a new spatial CUT&Tag method that converts chromatin-associated DNA into polyadenylated RNA via T7 linear amplification, allowing epigenetic profiling to be run on standard spatial transcriptomics platforms. Applied to mouse brain, it mapped activating and repressive chromatin marks, recovered region-specific regulatory programs, and correlated well with existing bulk and single-cell data. This lowers barriers to high-throughput spatial epigenomics by reusing widely available spatial workflows.

papers.title: Inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell perturbation data by optimizing causal reach of latent mediator dynamics.
papers.abstract: Resolving the causal structure of gene regulatory networks is central to understanding cellular regulation. Pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA readouts measure the transcriptional consequences of many interventions in parallel, providing a powerful resource for causal discovery. Combinatorial designs that perturb multiple regulators per cell increase throughput and can reveal responses that single-gene perturbations do not. However, inferring causal gene networks from these experiments remains challenging because gene regulatory interactions are nonlinear, dynamic, and often involve fe
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper presents a computational method for inferring causal gene regulatory networks from pooled CRISPR single-cell perturbation screens, including combinatorial perturbations. The approach models latent mediator dynamics and optimizes 'causal reach' to capture nonlinear, dynamic, and indirect regulatory interactions. This addresses a key challenge in causal discovery from perturbation data where effects are often mediated through intermediate genes.

papers.title: Mapping the regulatory wiring of endothelial cell differentiation reveals a critical role for Hippo mechanosignaling.
papers.abstract: At each step of development, stem cells encounter a branching decision to differentiate into one type of cell or another. This decision is executed through the action of competing gene programs that specify different cellular identities. Consequently, creating a comprehensive map of the gene programs that drive each branching step of human cell differentiation remains a long-sought goal of developmental and stem cell biology. Here, we introduce a framework combining genome-wide CRISPR screens, single-cell readouts, and gene program inference to systematically discover and characterize regulato
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present a framework that combines genome-wide CRISPR screens with single-cell readouts and gene program inference to systematically map the regulatory programs driving each branching step of human endothelial cell differentiation. Applying this approach, they identify Hippo mechanosignaling as a critical regulator of endothelial differentiation. The work provides a generalizable strategy for discovering regulators of cell fate decisions.

papers.title: OncoSpot enables benchmarking of cancer spatial transcriptomics methods across tumor evolutionary modes.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) is increasingly used to map clonal architecture within tumors, yet methods for analyzing cancer ST data are difficult to evaluate because real tumors lack ground truth for copy-number alterations (CNAs), subclonal identity, and malignant cell fraction. Existing ST simulators model normal tissue and do not represent tumor evolution, CNA-driven expression, or the spatial organization of malignant subclones. We present OncoSpot, a cancer-aware simulator of Visium-like spot-based ST data. OncoSpot combines a spatial evolutionary scaffold from DEMON, CNAs generated alon
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: OncoSpot is a cancer-aware simulator of Visium-like spatial transcriptomics data that models tumor evolution, CNA-driven expression, and spatial organization of malignant subclones, addressing the lack of ground truth in real tumor ST data. It combines a spatial evolutionary scaffold from DEMON with simulated CNAs to enable benchmarking of cancer ST analysis methods across different tumor evolutionary modes.

papers.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cell quality control.
papers.abstract: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present gcat and its_a_scam, two modular open-source tools for single-cell data processing and per-cell quality control. They argue that monolithic end-to-end pipelines limit flexibility and reproducibility, and offer these tools as composable alternatives that keep data usable beyond standard workflows.

papers.title: Comparative molecular analysis of histopathologic subtypes reveals shared epithelial remodeling yet distinct fibroblast programs in scleroderma lung disease.
papers.abstract: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) drives mortality in systemic sclerosis (SSc), with a subset developing progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) resembling idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Despite recognition of two distinct histopathologic patterns, the cellular basis of nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) and usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) remains poorly understood.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study compares the cellular and molecular features of two lung disease patterns (NSIP and UIP) seen in scleroderma patients, using single-cell and spatial approaches. It finds that epithelial remodeling is shared across both patterns, but the fibroblast programs differ distinctly between them. This suggests that the fibroblast compartment, rather than epithelial changes, may drive the divergent clinical trajectories of these histopathologic subtypes.

papers.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
papers.abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-di
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: VIGAT is a new tool that uses a vision-language model to automatically interpret ATAC-seq coverage plots and adaptively quantify gene activity from single-cell ATAC-seq data. By jointly examining accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes and integrating genomic annotations, it selects gene-specific regions that are more informative for distinguishing cell types than broadly accessible regions.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics of pediatric tuberculosis lymph nodes reveals a conserved hypoxia-SPP1 niche.
papers.abstract: Pediatric tuberculosis (TB) often presents as primary disease involving the mediastinal lymph nodes; however, its granuloma microenvironment remains poorly characterized because these population patient tissues are rarely available for study. Here, we use spatial transcriptomics to profile 60 granulomas from four children aged 4 to 36 months. We identified nine recurrent transcriptional microenvironments shared across granulomas, despite their marked histological heterogeneity. One macrophage-rich microenvironment showed strong hypoxia-associated activity and secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1) e
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using spatial transcriptomics on 60 granulomas from four young children with tuberculosis, researchers identified nine recurring tissue microenvironments despite substantial histological variation between granulomas. One macrophage-rich niche was consistently marked by hypoxia-associated gene activity and expression of secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), suggesting a conserved disease program across pediatric patients.

papers.title: DiffKnock: diffusion-based knockoff inference for neural networks with applications to single-cell RNA-sequencing data.
papers.abstract: High-throughput single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) technologies have revolutionized our ability to characterize cellular heterogeneity and dissect gene regulatory mechanisms. These data, however, are inherently high-dimensional and correlated, posing substantial challenges for statistical inference and feature selection. Identifying disease-related genes, while rigorously controlling false discoveries, remains a key challenge in scRNA-seq data analysis. Traditional methods often rely on parametric assumptions, which may fail to capture complex relationships and can suffer from inflated fal
papers.journal: Briefings in bioinformatics
papers.summary: DiffKnock introduces a diffusion-based knockoff inference framework for neural networks, designed to generate synthetic 'knockoff' features that mimic the correlation structure of real scRNA-seq data. This enables rigorous false discovery rate control during feature selection, addressing the limitations of parametric methods that struggle with high-dimensional, correlated single-cell data. The approach is applied to identify disease-related genes in scRNA-seq datasets.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell multi-omic data with graph-based topic modelling.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell biology enable the profiling of multiple molecular layers, such as the transcriptome, epigenome, and surface proteins, within a single cell. Tackling the complexity of these data from multiple perspectives allows researchers to gain the most comprehensive insights into cellular biological properties. Here, we propose a graph-based topic modelling method called bionSBM. Our method leverages well-known community-detection methods for multipartite graphs and the interpretability of topic modelling to cluster and explain high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cel
papers.journal: Briefings in bioinformatics
papers.summary: The paper introduces bionSBM, a graph-based topic modelling method for integrating single-cell multi-omic data across transcriptome, epigenome, and surface protein layers. It combines community-detection algorithms for multipartite graphs with topic modelling to cluster and interpret high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cell data. The approach aims to provide a more comprehensive view of cellular properties by jointly analyzing multiple molecular modalities.

papers.title: Age-based shifts in multicellular community organization and abundance in HPV-Negative Head and Neck Cancer.
papers.abstract: Aging represents a fundamental driver of cancer risk and progression, yet the mechanisms by which aging reshapes the tumor microenvironment remain incompletely understood. To interrogate how aging alters cellular and microenvironmental organization in cancer, we developed an integrated single-cell atlas of HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) encompassing 73 patients aged 18- 91 years. Using a multi-layered computational framework combining NMF-based module discovery and partial correlation network analysis, we reveal that age-associated differences in tumor composition a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors built an integrated single-cell atlas of HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma from 73 patients spanning ages 18–91 to study how aging reshapes the tumor microenvironment. Using NMF-based module discovery and partial correlation network analysis, they found that age is associated with shifts in tumor cellular composition and multicellular community organization. The work highlights aging as a driver of microenvironmental reorganization in cancer.

papers.title: Quantifying subcellular organization from localization to co-occurrence with InSpace.
papers.abstract: Cell identity and function depend not only on molecular abundance, but also on how molecules are organized within cells. Although spatial transcriptomics now resolves individual RNA molecules within cells, routine computational workflows reduce these measurements to cell-by-gene count matrices, retaining abundance while discarding information about intracellular localization and molecular co-occurrence. This loss of spatial information creates a need for scalable methods that preserve subcellular detail and enable comparisons across diverse cellular morphologies. Therefore, we present InSpace,
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: InSpace is a new computational tool that analyzes spatial transcriptomics data at the subcellular level, preserving information about where individual RNA molecules are located within cells and which molecules occur together, rather than collapsing data into standard cell-by-gene count matrices. This enables scalable comparison of intracellular organization across cells with diverse morphologies.

papers.title: SENgEAR: an interactive visualization platform for comparative analysis of senescence signatures and cellular communication.
papers.abstract: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets provide tremendous potential to identify the cellular states and communication networks associated with senescence. Annotating senescent cells in these datasets is hindered by the lack of universal markers for senescent cells and their context-dependent variability. To overcome this, several groups have developed gene signatures to annotate cells with distinct senotypes. However, comparing these signatures and their biological contexts to determine the specificity of senescence signatures remains complicated by the separate data platforms for sig
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SENgEAR is an interactive visualization platform that lets researchers compare different published gene signatures for cellular senescence and analyze how these signatures relate to cell-cell communication networks in single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. It addresses the problem that senescence lacks universal markers and that existing signatures are scattered across separate platforms, making specificity comparisons difficult.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.journal: Bio Systems
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe) so that the weight given to each method varies by regulator-target pair rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, the approach aims to resolve method disagreement at the edge level instead of choosing one method or averaging all.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.journal: Translational oncology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data from NSCLC patients to build a prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-derived genes, using machine learning to stratify patients by survival and immune activity. Low-PIS patients showed better outcomes and higher immune infiltration, and ADAM12 was identified and validated as a key functional regulator through cell line and mouse experiments. The work links epithelial cell states to immunotherapy response prediction in lung cancer.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.journal: Trends in genetics : TIG
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data into three groups: cell-type or single-cell resolution network inference, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability, and regulatory modulation. It highlights how spatial context enables more biologically grounded communication inference than scRNA-seq alone and maps methods to the distinct biological questions they address.

papers.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors introduce a Contextual Activity Score (CAS) that infers ADAR-associated RNA editing activity from gene expression data rather than raw sequencing reads, addressing the limitation of the standard Alu Editing Index (AEI) which cannot be applied to single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This enables estimation of ADAR activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial platforms using a unified expression-based framework.

papers.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.journal: Neuro-oncology
papers.summary: This study identifies NUDT21, a core component of the alternative polyadenylation (APA) machinery, as a key regulator in neuroblastoma. The authors show that NUDT21 orchestrates an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that sustains neuroblastoma cell proliferation and survival, revealing APA as a previously underappreciated regulatory layer in this pediatric cancer.

papers.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
papers.abstract: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. Here, we analyzed a pan-pediatric scRNA-seq atlas of 266 patient-and xenograft-derived samples across 22 pediatric solid
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors analyzed a pan-pediatric single-cell RNA-seq atlas of 266 samples across 22 pediatric solid tumor types to identify shared developmental gene expression programs. They found that pediatric sarcomas exhibit lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs, and used these programs to nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs for potential therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.
papers.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data used in epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often overlook hierarchical relationships among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across multiple simulated and real
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: HOMED is a new computational framework for DNA methylation deconvolution that improves estimation of cell-type proportions in bulk tissue samples. It incorporates hierarchical relationships among related cell types and uses single-cell RNA-seq plus paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data to optimize CpG signatures, addressing poor generalization of existing methods. The approach is validated across simulated and real datasets from multiple tissues.

papers.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical n
papers.journal: Cell systems
papers.summary: This review categorizes 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency (differentiation potential) from static scRNA-seq data into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based approaches. The authors analyze these methods under a unified mathematical framework, highlighting their differing and sometimes contrasting assumptions. The work provides guidance for choosing appropriate potency inference tools and clarifies the conceptual foundations of this emerging analysis paradigm.

papers.title: ETS1 as a Candidate Biomarker for Sepsis‑Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Multi‑Omics Analysis and Clinical Validation.
papers.abstract: This multi‑omics study aimed to screen candidate molecules associated with the transition from sepsis to sepsis‑associated ARDS, and provide preliminary biological evidence for risk‑stratification research.
papers.journal: Journal of inflammation research
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics analysis combined with clinical validation to identify ETS1 as a candidate biomarker associated with the transition from sepsis to sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The findings provide preliminary biological evidence supporting ETS1 for risk stratification in sepsis patients.

papers.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics via the Scissor algorithm reveals APOE-dependent cholesterol metabolic reprogramming in macrophages associated with osimertinib resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment contributes to acquired resistance against osimertinib in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the key cell subpopulations and the underlying metabolic mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated.
papers.journal: Frontiers in immunology
papers.summary: This study applies the Scissor algorithm to integrate bulk and single-cell transcriptomics and identify macrophage subpopulations linked to osimertinib resistance in NSCLC. The authors report that resistance is associated with APOE-dependent cholesterol metabolic reprogramming in macrophages, highlighting a microenvironment-driven metabolic mechanism.

papers.title: A ten-gene tyrosine-metabolism signature defines prognosis and reveals metabo-immune suppression in low-grade astrocytoma.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence implicates dysregulated tyrosine metabolism in glioma malignancy; however, its cell-type specificity and clinical relevance in low-grade astrocytoma (LGA) remain undefined.
papers.journal: PloS one
papers.summary: This study identifies a ten-gene signature related to tyrosine metabolism that can predict prognosis in low-grade astrocytoma. The signature also reveals a link between altered tyrosine metabolism and suppression of immune responses in the tumor microenvironment, suggesting a potential metabo-immune axis. The findings may help stratify patients and highlight metabolic targets for future therapies.

papers.title: Integrated bulk, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses identify Crot-associated proximal-tubule peroxisomal dysregulation in murine renal ischemia-reperfusion injury.
papers.abstract: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) underlies acute kidney injury after transplantation, shock, and major surgery. Proximal-tubule metabolic dysfunction shapes injury and repair. Peroxisomes shorten fatty acids and export products, but their cross-omic behavior in acute renal IRI remains unclear.
papers.journal: PloS one
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomics with proteomics to characterize proximal-tubule peroxisomal dysfunction in a mouse model of renal ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors identify Crot, a peroxisomal enzyme, as a key dysregulated factor associated with injury. The work provides a multi-omic map linking peroxisomal metabolism to acute kidney injury.

papers.title: A deep-learning microglial response score integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics for Alzheimer's disease stratification.
papers.abstract: Microglia exhibit diverse responses in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet linking these responses to tissue pathology and disease heterogeneity remains challenging. We aimed to develop a deep-learning microglial response score (DL-MRS) integrating single-cell, spatial and bulk transcriptomics to characterize AD-associated transcriptional patterns.
papers.journal: Frontiers in neuroscience
papers.summary: The authors present DL-MRS, a deep-learning-derived score that combines single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomic data to quantify microglial response states in Alzheimer's disease. This integrated score aims to stratify AD patients by microglial transcriptional patterns and link them to tissue pathology and disease heterogeneity.

papers.title: The predictive dermatome: a technical framework for spatial AI mapping of molecular skin aging.
papers.abstract: Skin aging is spatially heterogeneous. Chronological age and most systemic aging clocks provide useful population-level estimates, but they do not explain why adjacent or anatomically distinct skin regions may show different rates of dermal thinning, matrix remodeling, pigmentation change, vascular fragility, inflammation, or treatment response. We define the Predictive Dermatome as a computationally derived, anatomically localized skin region characterized by a shared or probabilistically related biological aging state and trajectory inferred from integrated molecular, structural, imaging, cl
papers.journal: Frontiers in digital health
papers.summary: This paper proposes the 'Predictive Dermatome' as a conceptual and technical framework for using spatial AI to map molecular skin aging. It argues that skin aging is spatially heterogeneous and that population-level aging clocks cannot capture regional differences in dermal thinning, pigmentation, inflammation, and treatment response. The framework integrates molecular, structural, and imaging data to define anatomically localized skin regions with shared or probabilistically related aging trajectories.

papers.title: A metabolic state in the cancer-associated fibroblast differentiation continuum of colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: The metabolic heterogeneity of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in the colorectal cancer (CRC) microenvironment remains poorly understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study investigates metabolic heterogeneity among cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in colorectal cancer, identifying a distinct metabolic state within the CAF differentiation continuum. The findings suggest that CAF metabolic programming is heterogeneous and may represent a targetable axis in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals cellular atlases and cell-cell interaction networks in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
papers.abstract: To summarize recent advances in single-cell multi-omics technologies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with a focus on cellular atlases, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication networks in hepatic and extrahepatic tissues.
papers.journal: Frontiers in pharmacology
papers.summary: This review summarizes how single-cell multi-omics technologies are being applied to MASLD, focusing on the construction of cellular atlases, characterization of cellular heterogeneity, and mapping of intercellular communication networks in both liver and extrahepatic tissues. It highlights how these approaches reveal disease-relevant cell states and interaction circuits that bulk profiling cannot resolve.

papers.title: Clinical and single-cell integration identifies a TCF21-associated stromal death-inflammation signature in endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Stromal heterogeneity, regulated-cell-death-associated stress, and chronic inflammation contribute to endometriosis, but their relationships within specific stromal populations remain incompletely understood. This study integrated clinical characterization with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to investigate a TCF21-associated stromal death-inflammation signature.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates clinical data with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize stromal heterogeneity in endometriosis, identifying a TCF21-associated stromal population linked to regulated cell death and chronic inflammation. The work proposes a 'death-inflammation signature' that may help explain how specific stromal subsets contribute to disease pathology.

papers.title: Multi-omics characterization of fibroblast subpopulations involved in osteogenic differentiation in periodontitis.
papers.abstract: Fibroblasts are the predominant stromal cells in periodontal tissues and are involved in inflammation and repair. However, their heterogeneity and molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Our study is to identify fibroblast subpopulations driving osteogenesis in periodontitis and their molecular markers.
papers.journal: Frontiers in physiology
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to identify distinct fibroblast subpopulations in periodontal tissue and characterize those that drive osteogenic differentiation during periodontitis. The authors propose molecular markers for these osteogenic fibroblast subsets, linking fibroblast heterogeneity to inflammation-associated bone formation in periodontal disease.

papers.title: Multi-source analysis identifies an NPC2-associated macrophage transcriptional program in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves extensive remodeling of intestinal macrophage states, but the molecular programs linking inflammation, lysosomal function, and lipid handling remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify macrophage-associated molecules and cellular states linked to UC.
papers.journal: Frontiers in immunology
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple data sources to identify a macrophage transcriptional program associated with NPC2, a lysosomal lipid-binding protein, in ulcerative colitis. The findings suggest that NPC2-expressing macrophages link inflammation with lysosomal function and lipid handling, highlighting a candidate molecular axis for further investigation in UC.
